rationale: clk_a and clk_b are declared without a clock group, so per ANALYSIS the relation is Unknown; equal periods, prose and the bench phase do not establish one. Every capture_b bit starts a clean depth-2 chain (capture_b -> data_o_r, line 11), so the author's CDC-004 cannot trigger: its predicate needs an unsynchronised destination bit. The source is src_a + data_i[0] (incrementing counter); the spec routes it to CDC-017 (counter heuristic, WARNING Heuristic for a non-async relation). CST-004 discloses the Unknown crossing; a CST-004 per-domain-pair instance names clocks, not this signal, so only its per-crossing instance can match. If the clocks are async, the word can be incoherent; if they are related, the path is timed, hence unknown. The class is clock_intent_inventory, matching both readers. Raw rst_n release, recovery/removal and physical timing remain external obligations outside this label.

labels.rationale: Distinct named 10 ns clocks have no declared relationship. Equal periods and one bench phase do not prove synchrony or exclusivity. capture_b followed by data_o_r supplies two destination stages per bit, but neither atomic bus transfer nor Gray/protocol qualification is established. The source is an incrementing binary counter, so carry transitions can be incoherently sampled.

clk_a and clk_b are separately declared with equal periods, but no relationship is declared. capture_b then data_o_r form two exact per-bit stages; this is independent bus synchronization, not a coherent transfer. Missing relationship prevents an established asynchronous defect or safe disposition. If asynchronous, arbitrary multi-bit source updates can yield mixed words. The arithmetic source has counter/carry structure, for which CDC-017 is the more specific published predicate.
